The four applications agree on the range, volume, alcohol content and per-can price while adapting information hierarchy to their stated service contexts.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

The identity and applications collectively support welcoming adult company at dinners, gatherings or evening cultural events. Typography, illustration, color and composition may take any coherent direction; literal people or dinner photography are optional. A dominant child-oriented or incompatible occasion positioning fails.

Where a physical can is pictured, its visible construction remains a cylindrical can with rounded shoulders and a pull-tab top, consistent with the supplied carrier. Applied artwork and camera angle may vary. Replacing the carrier with a different container fails; flat artwork and images without a can do not need to depict these features.

Public copy is English and preserves the supplied words, numbers and associations wherever required. Accept wrapping, capitalization changes and equivalent punctuation, including a time-range en dash. Missing words, changed quantities, mistranslations or altered meaning fail.

The supplied image inputs cover three distinct roles: can-panel-geometry.png is the constraint image, plain-can-lineup.png is the identity image of the existing undecorated product carrier, and evening-company.png is the atmosphere reference image. They are inputs rather than finished label designs or additional deliverables. This diagnostic does not require literal reproduction of the atmosphere reference.

A single specification page establishes the upstream design decisions as a record: adult evening positioning, the master logo, one unambiguous primary color code, typography, a named cue for each of the three flavors, the supplied descriptor and campaign line. Missing decisions or contradictory primary codes fail. The page records the identity rather than merely restating the delivery list.

The horizontal asset provides a horizontally arranged logo and the single-color asset uses one ink color, with background or negative space permitted. Both preserve the master logo's identifying forms and readable name. Recomposition is allowed; an unrelated mark or a multicolor single-color variant fails.

Each targeted application includes both specified public phrases and visibly uses the specification's primary color. Flavor accents and application-specific composition may vary. Omitting either phrase or replacing the primary color with an incompatible choice fails; ordinary rendering differences are acceptable.

All panels are flat portrait graphics with the specified 4:5 surface proportions and readable flavor name, 250 ml, 0.0% alcohol and Serve chilled. Citrus panels use Bright citrus, herbal finish.; berry panels use Red berry, floral finish.; pear panels use Soft pear, gentle spice. Their backs additionally use Citrus peel and rosemary., Red berries and hibiscus., and Pear and ginger., respectively. Each front/back pair shares its assigned specification cue. Front and back information hierarchy may differ; missing fields, wrong associations or inconsistent cues fail.

All four applications name the three flavors and state 250 ml, 0.0% alcohol and $4 per can. Both menus include Serve chilled. and complete matching records: Citrus & Rosemary—Bright citrus, herbal finish. / Citrus peel and rosemary.; Berry & Hibiscus—Red berry, floral finish. / Red berries and hibiscus.; Pear & Ginger—Soft pear, gentle spice. / Pear and ginger. The dinner menu supports seated reading, the tasting menu supports quick walk-up selection, and signs organize the range for shelf and counter contexts. Shared fields may be stated once. Missing records, wrong pairings or no meaningful adaptation to the stated service contexts fail.

Every poster and social visual contains the campaign line. Both event applications independently contain Evening, Together; Tasting evening; 10 October 2026; 18:00-21:00; The Glasshouse, 18 Willow Lane. Dinner applications feature and name Pear & Ginger in a dinner context; gathering applications feature and name Berry & Hibiscus in a gathering context. Launch social names all three flavors. Different layouts are allowed; incomplete event records, missing campaign lines or incorrect featured flavors fail.

Where a flavor appears, its visual cue remains recognizably associated with the same flavor in the specification and panel artwork. Multi-flavor pieces preserve three distinguishable assignments; single-flavor pieces preserve the featured flavor's cue. Scale, placement and simplification may vary. Swapped cues or replacement by an unrelated cue fail; applications are not required to introduce otherwise unrequested flavors.

Review the complete film and its duration: it runs 15 seconds and visibly reuses the delivered master logo, each of the three can fronts and launch-poster visuals. The brand name, descriptor and campaign line are readable during playback. It uses the specified primary color and preserves each flavor's cue. Animation, cropping and transitions may vary while source assets remain identifiable. Missing sources, incorrect runtime, unreadable required copy or changed flavor associations fail. Public copy remains English; any pictured can retains the supplied carrier's recognizable construction.
requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect complete SHA-bound original outputs. This source draft contains no completed professional or model-output review; partial-frame/page sampling cannot prove whole-output compliance.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation has at least ten pages and visibly reproduces every listed source, including identifiable stills from the delivered film. It repeats the specification's primary color code, descriptor, campaign line and three named flavor cues, preserves cue assignments, and includes a readable brand name. Sources may share pages and be resized if still identifiable. Mentioning an asset without showing it, substituting unrelated artwork, missing sources or fewer pages fails.

Logo variants retain the master logo's identifying forms, and all panels use the established identity. Front/back pairs preserve their assigned flavor cues, with three distinguishable flavors in one family.

Posters and social visuals share the established identity and retain specification cues wherever a flavor appears. Dinner communications feature Pear & Ginger, gathering communications feature Berry & Hibiscus, and both event applications carry the same complete event record.

Menus and signs preserve the established identity and all three flavor-to-cue assignments. The four applications agree on the range, volume, alcohol content and per-can price while adapting information hierarchy to their stated service contexts.
